findings.explanation: HOL4's collate has principal type ('a -> 'b -> ordering) -> 'a list -> 'b list -> ordering. Nothing in the four clauses equates the element types: f is only applied as f h1 h2. The reused names h and t in clauses 2 and 3 do not force equality, because Defn.defn_absyn_to_term (Defn.sml:1741-1799) excludes left-hand-side pattern variables from cross-clause unification and unifies only the head symbol and remaining free variables. Lean fixes both lists and f to one type α, so it is only the special case 'a = 'b. For example, collate (f : num -> bool -> ordering) [0] [T] = f 0 T is meaningful in HOL4 but cannot be stated in Lean.
findings.repair:
def collate {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f : α → β → Ordering) : List α → List β → Ordering
  | [], [] => EQUAL
  | [], _ :: _ => LESS
  | _ :: _, [] => GREATER
  | h1 :: t1, h2 :: t2 => if f h1 h2 = EQUAL then collate f t1 t2 else f h1 h2
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.Mllist

example : ∀ (α : Type) (f : α → α → Ordering), @Candle.Mllist.collate α f [] [] = Ordering.eq := by
  intro α f
  simp [Candle.Mllist.collate]
findings.hol4_check: !(f:num -> bool -> ordering). mllist$collate f [0n] [T] = f 0n T
